findings.problem: The design claims the chat-send credential guard fires 'before any row is created'. Verified: the message row is created only after the cred check, so the claim holds for the message row, but the conversation upsert runs BEFORE the credential block, so a decrypt-throw/missing-creds path still writes/updates a conversation row while returning 500. This is pre-existing behavior unchanged by the rewire (not a regression); only the sentence is imprecise.
findings.fix: Reword §9.2 to 'no message row is created before the guard; the conversation upsert already runs earlier and is unchanged by this rewire', OR move the resolveSendCredentials try/catch wrap above the conversation upsert so a credential failure returns 500 before any DB write.

findings.problem: Manual path hardcodes tokenExpiresAt: null and does not introspect expiry, so a pasted short-lived user token will silently stop working later with no UI signal. Mitigated by §5.1 helper text recommending a System User token.
findings.fix: Keep the behavior but document the gotcha in §5.2 and scratchpad.md: 'a temporary token stored manually will stop working at Meta's expiry; no proactive expiry tracking', consistent with the out-of-scope token-refresh decision.

findings.problem: AC #15 literally names META_CONFIG_ID in .env.example; the design intentionally keeps only NEXT_PUBLIC_META_CONFIG_ID (config id is read solely by FB.login in the browser). Defensible placement, but diverges from the literal AC text.
findings.fix: Leave as designed; ensure .env.example/scratchpad.md state explicitly that the Embedded Signup Configuration ID lives as NEXT_PUBLIC_META_CONFIG_ID and that this satisfies AC #15's intent, so no later reader re-adds a dead server mirror.
